title: Each tab keeps its own in-memory list and writes all of it back, so a second tab silently erases the first tab's recipes
evidence: `recipes` is read once at app.js:3. The add handler (app.js:23-24) and the delete handler (app.js:34-35) save the whole in-memory array. Nothing re-reads storage before saving and nothing listens for the `storage` event.
failing_case: Open the page in tab A and tab B, both showing 2 recipes. Add 'Pie' in tab B (storage now has 3). Add 'Stew' in tab A. A saves its own 2 + 'Stew', so storage has 3 recipes and 'Pie' is gone. Neither tab shows an error.
remediation: Before each mutation, re-read storage and apply the change to that fresh list. Also handle `window.addEventListener('storage', ...)` to reload and re-render.

title: Delete ignores the save result and always reports 'Deleted'
evidence: saveRecipes returns false on failure (store.js:13-20). The add handler checks it (app.js:24-25), but the delete handler at app.js:35 discards it and then sets `Deleted “…”.` at app.js:36.
failing_case: Storage rejects the write (blocked, quota, or a private-mode setItem that throws). The user deletes 'Soup' and sees 'Deleted “Soup”.'. On reload, getItem still returns the old list and 'Soup' is back. The message reported a delete that was never saved.
remediation: Use the result: `if (!saveRecipes(recipes)) statusEl.textContent = 'Couldn't save the deletion...'` with the same wording and next step as the add path, and keep the 'Deleted' message only for the success branch.

quote: // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Corrupt or unreadable storage loads as an empty list, nothing tells the user, and the next save overwrites the original data
evidence: store.js:6-10 returns [] on a JSON.parse error or a getItem error, and store.js:7 silently drops every entry without a string name. The comment says app.js tells the user. app.js:3 calls `loadRecipes()` and uses the result as-is. No other line in app.js reads a load failure, so nothing is ever shown. The first successful add then runs saveRecipes (app.js:24), which writes over the key.
failing_case: localStorage 'recipes' holds `[{"name":"Soup","minutes":20,"id":"1"},` (truncated by a crash, or a hand edit), or a transient getItem exception. The page opens with 'No recipes yet'. The user adds one recipe. setItem replaces the damaged value with a 1-item list, and the original recipes are gone with no warning and no way back. Entries without a string name are dropped the same way on the next save.
remediation: Make loadRecipes return `{list, error}`. On a parse error, keep the raw string under a backup key, show a message in #status, and do not overwrite the key until the user has been told. Count dropped entries and report them.

title: After a keyboard delete the focused button is destroyed and focus drops to the page start
evidence: The delete handler calls `render()` (app.js:37). render replaces `listEl.innerHTML` (app.js:10), which removes the focused Delete button. Nothing moves focus afterwards. Traced; the browser resets focus to body when the focused element is removed. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to the Delete button on the 5th recipe, presses Enter and confirms. Focus goes to body, so the next Tab starts again at the first control and the user has to tab past every remaining recipe. The status message is announced, but the position is lost.
remediation: After deleting, focus the next row's Delete button, or the previous one, or the 'Your recipes' heading (with tabindex=-1) when the list is empty.

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: Loader checks only `name`; a saved record without `id` or a numeric `minutes` makes Delete throw and the total read NaN
evidence: The filter at store.js:7 keeps any object with a string name. render (app.js:10) writes `data-id="undefined"` for a record with no id. The delete handler (app.js:32) compares `x.id === "undefined"`, which matches nothing, so `r` is undefined. `describe(r)` (app.js:33 calls app.js:15) then reads `recipe.name` on undefined and throws a TypeError. The comment at app.js:14 says it is never null, which this case contradicts. totalMinutes (store.js:23) adds `r.minutes`: undefined gives NaN, and a string '20' gives string concatenation.
failing_case: localStorage 'recipes' = `[{"name":"Soup"}]`, written by an earlier version or a hand edit. The list shows 'Soup NaN min'. Clicking Delete throws an uncaught TypeError and the record cannot be removed from the UI. Adding any recipe shows 'Total cooking time: NaN minutes'. With `minutes` stored as the string '20', the total becomes '020' followed by the next number, concatenated.
remediation: Add one normaliser at the storage boundary. It keeps a record only if `name` is a non-empty string, makes `minutes` a finite positive number, and assigns a fresh id if one is missing. Also make the delete handler return early when `r` is undefined.
